## Historical audit: S0241

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/audit_sources/raw_failures/scene_rsi_v2_2/r1/fixed_h/H0/fixed_version_test/commons_92056365/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. The supplied observations contain complete lines, so split-observation offsets are not applicable.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — student request, line 1 | Reconstruct one 512 × 379 indoor reference photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching viewpoint and framing. The reference image itself is not visible in the supplied text. |
| Initial build — student response and execution, lines 3–4 | The student inferred a windowed dining room and programmed repeated tables, chairs and booths, architecture, pendants and foliage. Furniture and lamp components were grouped as assets; grouping does not establish physical connection. Chair facing parameters and plant orientations encode poses, but their correctness is unverified. Colored primitives and geometric floor seams approximate finishes; there is no evident image-texture use. A camera, three area lights and grayscale compositor were specified. |
| First validation — execution result, line 5 | The build failed after about 392 seconds at `world.color`: the scene world was `None`. The result reported `image: null`; no visual comparison was possible. This is a concrete execution failure, not evidence that the scene matched or mismatched. |
| Feedback and revision — student request/response, lines 6–9 | The student received the execution traceback, not teacher feedback or a rendered image. The revised program creates a world if absent, simplifies floor seams and replaces Boolean pendant shades with generated mesh surfaces; it retains the camera, lighting and grayscale approach. The second program was actually executed. |
| Final validation — execution result, line 10 | The second execution timed out after about 29.8 seconds, with empty stdout/stderr and `image: null`. The trace establishes neither that the world fix completed nor where this attempt spent its time. |

**Outcome and exploration.** The visible outcome is an initial program error followed by a technical timeout; no successful build or render is recorded. This is not an empty patch: a substantial revision was submitted and run. Two student sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 and 7); the two runner executions are visible, but there is no evidence of autonomous external exploration or a rendered-view review. No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, input, or adoption is visible; the traceback is runner feedback.

**Transfer and uncertainty.** The transferable operational lesson is that a missing Blender world can halt an otherwise extensive build, while a timeout gives no diagnosis without further evidence. The room layout, monochrome treatment and proposed geometry are task-specific hypotheses, not independently verified facts. In particular, object count and placement, materials and textures, component contact, pose, camera framing, illumination and rendered appearance remain unresolved: neither the reference pixels nor a successful rendered image are available in this audit.
